reviews.text: I visited the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding today and it was an absolutely heart-warming and memorable experience. Arriving in the morning was the perfect choice, as many pandas were active—eating bamboo, climbing, playing, and lazing around in their beautifully designed, natural-style enclosures. The entire park is lush, peaceful, and well maintained, with shaded walking paths, streams, and clear signage that make exploring comfortable and enjoyable. The red pandas added an extra dose of charm. Informational displays throughout the base explain conservation and breeding efforts in an engaging and educational way, making the visit feel meaningful rather than just sightseeing. Although it can get crowded later in the day, the overall organization is good and the experience is well worth it. A must-visit in Chengdu for anyone who loves nature, wildlife, and conservation. 🐼

Visiting this place was one of the highlights of my time in Chengdu. The park is large, lush, and beautifully designed, with plenty of greenery, bamboo forests, and walking paths that make the experience feel more like a nature reserve than a typical zoo. It’s very well maintained, clean, and easy to navigate, though you should be prepared for quite a bit of walking. The main attraction, of course, is the giant pandas. Seeing them up close was truly special, watching them eat bamboo, climb trees, play, or simply lounge around is surprisingly calming. The best time to visit is early in the morning, as the pandas are much more active before midday. By late morning or afternoon, many of them tend to nap, which is still cute but less engaging. Beyond the pandas, the research base does a good job emphasizing conservation, education, and breeding efforts. There are informative displays explaining panda behavior, habitats, and the challenges of protecting this endangered species. This adds depth to the visit and makes it feel meaningful, not just entertaining. There are also red pandas, which are incredibly charming and worth spending time with. That said, some viewing areas can feel congested, so patience is definitely needed. Facilities like rest areas, cafes, and souvenir shops are available, though food options are fairly basic. Overall, this is a must-visit attraction that offers a mix of education, conservation awareness, and pure joy. Whether you’re a wildlife lover or just curious, it’s a memorable experience that gives you a deeper appreciation for pandas and the efforts made to protect them. Visiting early and planning your route ahead will help you get the most out of your time there.

Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding 🐼 The pandas here are unbelievably cute, from playful babies to chill adult pandas. I watched them playing and resting - it truly felt like a dream come true for any panda lover. The atmosphere is airy, spacious, and pleasantly cool, perfect for a relaxing walk. I also loved the panda-themed café and the unique panda souvenirs inside (you can’t easily find anywhere else) Definitely a must-visit spot in Chengdu!💕

A must-visit place in Chengdu The Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding is a must-visit attraction if you are in Chengdu. The park is spacious, clean, and well-maintained, with a natural environment designed to suit the pandas. Seeing giant pandas up close is truly special, especially in the morning when they are more active and feeding. The walking paths are well organised, and there are clear signs in both Chinese and English, making it easy for visitors to navigate around the base. The base is not only a tourist attraction but also an important centre for panda conservation, research, and education. It is suitable for families, students, and anyone interested in wildlife and nature conservation. Tip: Visit early in the morning to avoid crowds and to see the pandas at their most active.

A visit to the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding is an absolute delight and a must-do when in Sichuan. It offers a rare and heartwarming opportunity to see these gentle giants up close in a beautifully maintained, naturalistic environment. Watching the pandas, from playful cubs tumbling around to adults contentedly munching on bamboo, is an incredibly charming experience. The base is not just a zoo but a world-renowned conservation center dedicated to panda research and breeding. Tip: Arrive early in the morning, around opening time, as this is when the pandas are most active and feeding. It gets very crowded later in the day.

This is gonna be a brutal review and if you want to know how to plan your day, read this: The park was huge, big and massive. The fee was ¥55 bookable with agencies. Another ¥30 for shuttle carts if you don’t wanna walk. The park was big and minimal and confusing direction. I chose to walk and manage to get out the park within 4 hours. Yes literally 4 hours of walking and marking around. You will see a lot of pandas. Most of them are sleeping. Like another zoo, but the main characters are panda. Red panda section was closed during my visit.

The Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding is a major attraction where you can see many pandas. I recommend visiting in the early morning (between 7:30 AM and 10:00 AM) to maximize your chances of seeing them while they are active, as they tend to sleep later in the morning and throughout the afternoon. To save time, I opted to pay extra for the internal tour bus. This allows you to easily hop on and off at various stations, which is very helpful since the park is quite large. Unfortunately, I decided against queuing to see the famous panda Hua Hua (花花). Even though it was off-peak in early January, the wait time was over an hour. I made this choice based on advice from my tour driver, who mentioned that Hua Hua is simply a smaller and chubbier panda compared to her peers. I hope I don’t regret prioritizing my time over seeing her in person. Overall, a 3-hour visit is sufficient for navigating the park, even for a family with young children around age 10.

We arrived early in the morning aiming to catch the panda feeding time, but in reality it did not make a huge difference. The pandas were actively eating well into late morning, roughly until around 11am. While a few had already settled down to sleep, most were still moving about, eating, or interacting, so there was plenty to see even if you do not arrive right at opening. One downside in the early morning was visibility. On cooler, more humid mornings the glass enclosures fog up quite badly in some areas, making it difficult to see the pandas clearly. This was a bit frustrating, especially when you are trying to take photos or watch them up close. The layout and map could also be improved. The map is not very intuitive and it is easy to lose your bearings. I found myself constantly checking directions to avoid walking in circles or backtracking. Clearer signage or better wayfinding would significantly improve the experience. That said, the overall experience was still fantastic. The center is beautifully maintained, spacious, and you genuinely get to see a large number of giant pandas across different enclosures. There are also red pandas, which were a lovely bonus and just as entertaining to watch. I did hear about another, quieter panda base in Dujiangyan, about an hour and twenty minutes away. While it sounds appealing for those wanting a less crowded experience, the travel time felt too long for us. You could technically combine that area with visits to the nearby temple and the Dujiangyan irrigation system, but seeing pandas alone is easily a full day activity. Overall, despite a few logistical annoyances, this is an amazing conservation center and absolutely worth visiting if you are in Chengdu. Seeing so many pandas in one place is a memorable experience.

The Panda Base is extremely large, if you want to go whole this area, it will cost you at least a day. You can buy ticket on Trip with price around 7.5$ (not included shuttle bus). You can buy shuttle bus ticket at South gate of IFS Tower (Chungxi road), price around 1.6$ / route. You should take the first bus start at 7:30 am everyday to get to this base earliest as you can. That time visitors are not crowded, so you can meet and take photos with Pandas easily

The Panda Breeding Center in Chengdu, China is one of the most heartwarming and unique places I’ve ever visited. It’s not just a zoo — it’s a research and conservation center where you can see giant pandas being cared for, bred, and protected in a natural, peaceful environment. The moment you enter, the atmosphere feels calm and green, surrounded by bamboo forests and clean walking paths. The pandas are the real stars here — you can see them eating bamboo, climbing trees, and even rolling around lazily. Watching baby pandas playing together is the most adorable sight imaginable!

Chengdu is undisputed as the world's panda capital. While there are two conservation parks, the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding (成都熊猫基地) is the best option with more Panda and it's home most of the celebrity Pandas. The Experience The pandas are absolutely adorable and too cute to resist. You will see them doing all kinds of funny stunts to find a sleeping spot on the trees. There's signage indicating the panda residents for each enclosure, together with brief introduction for each panda, so you'll know which panda you are seeing. However, be mentally prepared for the crowds and pushing at the viewing areas—everyone wants that perfect shot. 🐼 The Celebrity: Hua Hua The Panda base is home to Hua Hua, the world's most popular panda, located at Villa 6. Note that Hua Hua is off duty every Monday. You won't get to see her, but the park will generally be less crowded. 🗼 Panda Tower (熊猫塔) Free access, but advance booking is required. It is closed on Tuesdays or during unfavorable weather conditions. ⏰ Arrive Early The park opens at 7:30 AM. Getting there right at opening is the single best way to beat the crowds and catch the pandas while they are active and eating breakfast. 🚪 Choose Your Gate * South Gate: The most popular entrance. Closest to Villa 6 (Hua Hua's home) and the nurseries, but gets the most crowded. * West Gate: The newer entrance. Generally quieter with a more scenic route. 🚇 Public Transport (Subway Line 3) * To South Gate: Stop at Panda Avenue Station (熊猫大道). Take Exit D, turn right, and catch shuttle bus 408 (¥2, scan QR to pay upon boarding). * To West Gate: Stop at Chengdu Junqu General Hospital Station (军区总医院) and take shuttle bus 409 (¥2). 📝 Essential Tips * Tickets (¥55/adult): Book online 7 days in advance (via WeChat mini program or Trip.com) as there is a daily cap. * Park Shuttle (¥30): The base is massive. Definitely take the shuttle to save energy. * Come Prepared: Apply sunscreen and wear flat shoes. Even with the shuttle, you will be doing a lot of walking. * Lower your voice and avoid using flash: Pandas are sensitive to noise and flash light.

amazing experience. We got to see the pandas and their babies. Unfortunately only for a small amount of time since it got hot pretty soon and pandas don't like hot temperatures. So I recommend you going there when the weather is a bit cooler. Prepare to go early in the morning. Pandas will be out for some time before they go to sleep. We arrived around 10:30 am and most of the pandas were already sleepy. It was also interesting to see the red pandas.

Absolutely incredible l. It was everything I dreamed of and more. World class zoo type place. Heaps of enclosures for different weather, full of natural elements for the animals. Stunning grounds full of beautiful forests and gardens. Amenities everywhere to meet a wide range of needs. Excellent food options, interpreter options, shuttle buses and exhibits. Had perfect cool weather, animals were very active.

Nice place for visit in Chengdu from children to adult. This place is huge, every parts of the park must travel by a park - bus. Each section have different things to vist. Panda stay every where in the park, you can walk and take picture with them very easy. They are all awake, eating bamboo from adult panda to baby panda. In this park they also have multiple of shop that visitor can buy goods and restaurant with panda theme.

Easily accessible from Chengdu either by bus or taxi. Close up with pandas in their enclosures. You will be entertained by the playful characteristics of the pandas. You can also see red pandas. Do go in the morning as pandas are more actives. There's a rest area where you can enjoy drinks or food

Amazing experience, doesn't feel like a zoo as the animals need help to survive and are given a big space with large amounts of food (bamboo) daily and are surrounded by nature that is their own! There are also many red pandas! I very much suggest it as a visit when you're in Chengdu.

The universe doesn’t need more proof of perfection, but here it is. Pandas eating, sleeping, and occasionally rolling downhill like fuzzy boulders. Red pandas sneaking around trees, also eating because clearly that’s a species-wide policy. And the humans? We join the cult willingly, buying panda-shaped ice cream, panda hats, panda buns. It’s not a zoo, it’s a black-and-white lifestyle brand. Even the trash bins have ears. Everywhere you look, someone’s smiling, someone’s taking 200 identical photos, and a panda’s chewing like a philosopher who’s found peace in carbohydrates. The air smells of bamboo and faint existential joy. 5/5. You don’t visit Chengdu Panda Base. You surrender to it.

A wet and rainy day...the last few days were scorching hot hovering 35 to 37 Deg C and it was 24 deg C when we visited. Windy, cold and Panda Watching was fun and yet cold. Beautiful place. Serene in certain areas, lovely plants and beautiful bamboo everywhere. The whole place was clean, efficient staff, and very admirable for the work that they put up over the years. Do book tickets online. We have problems booking the tickets online and our service apartment staff used her handphone to do the booking .
This park is spacious and environment friendly. Some pandas are even order than me. There is a souvenir shop near the entrance where you can buy gifts.

The Panda Research Base in Chengdu is an absolute must-see. After all, who wouldn't want to watch adorable pandas munching on bamboo and being clumsy and adorable? It's conveniently located just outside the city center and has a very affordable entry fee. My only recommendation is to do a little research beforehand; the base is huge, so knowing where you want to go will help you avoid getting lost and make the most of your time

Fantastic place to visit pandas 🐼 , lived up to my expectation . It is a very big location. Buying the band for the transport buggies is well worth the little money . Great viewing points to see the pandas .. pro tips - go early & in the colder weather . Sichuan Province .. pandas everywhere 🫶

I visited the Chengdu Panda Base and it was absolutely wonderful! 🐼 The highlight of my trip was seeing Huahua, the star panda, happily munching on bamboo. 🌿 Such an unforgettable experience — the pandas are so adorable and well cared for. Highly recommend visiting if you’re in Chengdu!

Very very large park with multiple pandas residing here. The park is huge hence be prepared to walk. Not all pandas are viewable given the weather condition. Some will be indoors within air conditioned enclosures and not available for viewing during hot days. Managed to see 1 who was chilling in running water. There is also a red panda which is a smaller species. Retails sales is brisks. We got some within the park and bought more outside at the stall. The latter price is a lot cheaper hence withstand the urge until you have exited the park.
It was amazing to see pandas in real life! It has always been my dream. It was very crowded though due to holidays coming soon (Chinese New Year)

We only saw a small part of the big 25Hectare site as our hosts (the city of Chengdu as part of the UNESCO Festival of Intangible Cultural Heritage) treated us to this wonderful morning visit there. However, we did see several panda, mostly juvenile and the museum and loved both. We did not go through the main entrance so I cant comment on that but we did have a English speaking guide. If I ever go back to Chengdu (maybe) I'd love to spend a whole day there as they also have Red Panda which I love:-) This was in June so not sure if that is considered shoulder season. We were told that the wait at the most famous panda He Hua was 3 hours on the day we were there, so I guess it can get very busy there.

The famous Panda Base in Chengdu is an unmissable attraction for anyone visiting the city. Renowned for its work in panda conservation, the park offers a rare opportunity to see a large number of giant pandas and red pandas up close in a naturalistic environment. These adorable animals are undoubtedly the highlight of the visit, as you can observe them eating, playing, and lounging in specially designed enclosures that mimic their natural habitat. In addition to the pandas, the base also features a museum that provides an educational experience, offering insights into panda biology, conservation efforts, and the research conducted at the facility. This makes it a great destination for both animal lovers and those looking to learn more about these iconic creatures. The park itself is massive, with sprawling paths that wind through lush greenery and mountain terrain. To make the most of your visit, it’s highly recommended to pay for the shuttle service, which conveniently transports visitors between key areas of the park. Without the shuttle, you might spend hours walking through the extensive grounds, which can be tiring, especially on a hot day. Whether you’re traveling with family, friends, or solo, the Chengdu Panda Base promises a memorable experience filled with both fun and education. Make sure to plan ahead and allocate enough time to fully explore this incredible conservation park.

Lots of areas to cover. Unfortunately we came on a Monday and was unaware that Hua Hua's enclosure is closed on Mondays! But nonetheless it was an fun experience. Lots of sleepy pandas to take pics of -- including ones that climb to the top of a tree branch! Red pandas are equally as cute. They had star monkeys too but their enclosure was temporarily closed.

Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地) is a must-visit in Chengdu. Pandas are truly cute and adorable creatures — they basically eat, sleep, and poop all day! Expect cuteness overload, with some pandas pulling off the silliest and most entertaining moves. Tickets can be purchased via WeChat if you have a local number. Otherwise, you can also buy them onsite with your passport — there might be a short queue, but it is manageable. The park is huge, with plenty of resting benches and food stalls. We spent around 3 hours walking through the whole place. Shuttle rides are also available for a small fee if you prefer not to walk too much. Be sure to check out the breeding centre — it is both fun and educational!

Once you get past the gates and the crowds it a beautiful open space with Panda enclosers throughout. If walking the park come perpeared for a few hill climbs, but the scenery makes it all worth it. The view from the Bamboo tower is amazing, again prepear for a lot of stairs. Overall well worth a visit.

I was really impressed by the panda research base. Not only did I get to see a lot more pandas than I expected, the place was beautiful and very well taken care of. The pandas seemed happy and healthy, too. The base is huge and I only saw a part of it, but I'm glad I went and would gladly recommend it to others! It's fairly easy to get around using English here.

Great experience to visit giant pandas and red pandas in a near natural environment. We arrived early in the morning and watched pandas feed and sleep. The park is very nicely established and promote walking in beautiful sceneries. Entering from south entrance and leaving north exit we had a near full day in beautiful Chengdu, China.

Very beautifull and big park! I reccomend taking the available mini-busses to get around otherwise you will need to walk alottt, it wasn't very crowded when i went. [Around afternoon] but be aware it closes around 17:30.

I think it’s a good place to explore and it’s nicely made and informative but don’t bother to go during the summer months if it’s hot! All giant pandas will be indoors which makes the whole experience like a zoo visit with hundreds of people trying to get a nice photo/video through the glas wall. Only red pandas would be outdoors. If you in Chengdu and temperatures are above 26 degrees Celsius, skip the trip.

The place was really big and I saw so many pandas for the first time in my entire life. The center isn't fully about just great pandas it also has a different section for red pandas. The pandas were either eating or sleeping here. Wherever you spotted a crowd just know that a panda is doing some activity there, people don't usually look at the sleeping ones for a long time or in crowds. It was such a nice place with such nice vibes to it.

Like Disneyland but for pandas! The place was huge and well-built/organized. The pandas seemed relatively happy in their homes and taken care of. Would definitely recommend wearing comfortable shoes to visit though since a lot of walking is necessary!!!

If you wants to see red or giant panda, you have to visit it. There is electricity car to go up and back to the hill but have to wait to much (30-40 minutes)!! The area is extremly in good conditions like a golf playing ground.

Wow! This is such an amazing facility for the preservation of the giant pandas. It offers a unique opportunity to see a large number of pandas up close in a well-maintained environment, learn about their conservation efforts, and witness their playful behavior; however, be prepared for crowds and plan to go early to avoid the rush. The Chengdu Panda Research Base is renowned for having one of the largest captive panda populations in the world, allowing you to see a variety of pandas at different ages and stages. We saw young playful ones through adults. Beyond just viewing pandas, the research base provides information about their conservation status, breeding programs, and the challenges they face in the wild. We were really impressed by how beautiful and well organized the large facility is. The panda enclosures are designed to mimic their natural environment, creating a comfortable viewing experience. One potential downside is we were told that the popularity of the site can lead to very large crowds during peak seasons. We fortunately visited in late December, and while it was busy, the crowds were manageable. My kids also appreciated the food court & restrooms with western style sit down toilets. And be sure to visit the souvenir shop for some adorable keepsakes.

We prefer the zones near the West gate (the area I circled in red), more pandas and the living environment is like VIP, whereas most of the crowds are at South Gate, as the celebrity panda HuaHua is there. Transport:better take the Panda Shuttle to reach right in front of the entrance. Taxis can only drop off at the point about 800m away. Time to visit: recommended early in the morning, as pandas need to go indoor once temperature go over 26 Celsius. Breeding season is August to September, so plan your visit well if new-born panda is what u wanna see. In-park shuttle bus: not really recommend to buy that shuttle ticket, as the shuttle stops are very poorly planned. It will only waste you more time to find the boarding point, and during the peak hour, queue is looooong and no empty cars… Better plan a full day here, slowly taking your time to walk the park through. Food: better bring your easy food or snacks. There are restaurants inside, but my experience wasn’t nice so I don’t recommend to dine inside.
We reached early… because timing matters here. Nearly 4 hours here, and it still wasn’t enough. The place is huge, and so many pandas to see.
If you want to see pandas that aren't lying around and sleeping, you have to enter as soon as the park opens because that is when they are having breakfast and most active.

Our visit to the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding was absolutely enchanting — a perfect blend of conservation, culture, and cuteness overload. ⸻ 🐼 Highlights • The base is home to over 170 giant pandas, including playful babies in the nursery and majestic adults lounging in bamboo forests ￼. • Watching pandas between 8:30–10 AM, during feeding time, rewards you with the most lively and engaging sightings ￼. • Well-designed enclosures and shaded pathways beautifully recreate natural habitats — there are even red pandas, black swans, and peacocks to discover ￼. ⸻ 🛠 Visitor Experience • Booking tickets online with real-name registration via WeChat or other platforms ensures a smooth entry — essential due to capacity controls ￼. • Arriving before 7:30 AM gives you an edge on crowds at both the entrance and key panda zones ￼. • A hop-on/hop-off shuttle bus (10 RMB) helped us explore the sprawling 238-hectare site comfortably ￼. ⸻ 👍 Pros & 👎 Cons 👍 Pros: • Close-up panda interactions, especially with cubs — their playful antics will melt your heart. • Educational exhibits including a museum, nursery viewing windows, Panda Tower, and conservation-focused displays ￼ ￼. • Family-friendly amenities: cafes, snacks near Swan Lake, gift shops, and stroller-accessible paths (). 👎 Cons: • The base gets extremely crowded, especially on weekends and holidays — weekdays and early mornings are best ￼. • Cafes open late (around 11 AM) — bring water and snacks if you arrive early (). • It’s a large site, so expect at least 3–4 hours of walking; shuttle buses are handy ￼. ⸻ 🌟 Final Verdict The Chengdu Panda Base is the ultimate panda pilgrimage. From the joy of watching baby pandas roll and munch to the deeper appreciation of conservation efforts, it’s a thoroughly memorable experience. Ideal for families, wildlife lovers, and anyone wanting a heartwarming adventure outside Chengdu. 👍 Tips for Future Visitors 1. Book entry 7 days ahead and choose early morning tickets. 2. Target 8–10 AM for peak panda activity. 3. Take the shuttle bus to cover more ground with less fatigue. 4. Bring your own snacks or wait for café opening times (~11 AM). 5. Opt for weekdays if you prefer fewer crowds. ⸻ Sample Google Review: 5 stars 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 A magical morning with China’s national treasures! The Chengdu Panda Base is everything you dream of—playful pandas of all ages, beautiful bamboo habitats, and charming red pandas too. We arrived early (highly recommended!) and caught the pandas during their feeding frenzy around 8:30 AM—absolutely adorable. The shuttle bus helped navigate the large park, and educational exhibits added depth to the visit. Bring water/snacks since cafes open late. Whether you’re with family or solo, this place is a heartfelt, unforgettable journey into the world of giant pandas.
Went late-June and we saw a handful of pandas, mostly young ones in both the outdoor and indoor enclosures. The area is massive and requires you to walk and trek a lot. It is a must visit in Chengdu.

The weather was insanely hot during my visit, around 36 degrees during hot sunny day. So it was almost impossible to see panda outdoor, since panda couldn't stand hot temperature. So we can only see panda in indoor room with AC. A bit dissapointed though, but I got too see one panda pooing and scrub the butt, so adorable.. This place is very neat and well taken care off. Free shuttle bus can take you around. There's also souvenir shop with so many cute panda plushies

This expansive breeding facility provides an opportunity to see giant and red pandas close up in enclosures resembling their normal habitat. On this warm October day they could be seen up in the trees, mostly sleeping. I’m told they are more active when it’s cooler. Workers also brought cubs out from the nursery and bottle fed them. Apparently their mothers often stop nursing in captivity. It was all very cute. You can also pay to hold a panda and have your picture taken. I chose not to. It is attractive and well maintained with plenty of gift shops and informal fast food type dining. Because of the park’s large size I would advise shuttle tickets. We found they were difficult to purchase after entering the park (you purchase by phone and need a chinese ID and phone number). Probably best to buy online before coming. It was hot, hilly and humid and I walked 28,000 steps!

Visiting the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding is an unforgettable experience. The facility allows you to observe rare giant pandas and red pandas up close as they play, sleep, and eat in a beautifully maintained environment filled with bamboo forests. The park is expansive, but a shuttle service is available for those who prefer not to walk. Additionally, you can purchase genuine stuffed toy pandas from their official store as souvenirs. Pandas are most active during feeding time, typically between 7:30 AM and 10:00 AM. Arriving early will enhance your chances of witnessing their lively behavior. The base operates daily from 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM. Entrance fee is CNY 55 per person, with ticket sales and checking available from 7:30 AM to 5:00 PM. The base is located approximately 18 km north of Chengdu’s city center. You can take a taxi, which takes about 30-40 minutes, or use public transportation options. A donation center is available for those interested in contributing to panda conservation efforts. The park also offers a shuttle service for easier navigation. Overall, the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding provides an exceptional opportunity to connect with these magnificent creatures in a serene and well-preserved setting.

🐼 Chengdu Giant Panda Base – A Must-Visit, But Get Ready to Walk! 🚶‍♂️ Visiting the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding was an unforgettable experience! 🐼❤️ The place is huge, and I definitely got my steps in because the attractions are quite spread out. I had to walk a lot (including climbing up a hill 🥲), but honestly, it was all worth it. Unfortunately, I couldn’t buy a buggy car ride since I don’t have WeChat Pay, which made things a bit tougher. But hey, at least I got a solid workout! 😅 The real highlight? The pandas, of course! Seeing them up close was absolutely magical. The red pandas stole my heart—they’re so adorable and active! 🦊🐾 Definitely a bucket list experience checked! ✅ If you’re planning to visit, be prepared for lots of walking, but trust me—it’s all part of the adventure. Would I do it again? 100% YES! 🎋🐼

Wow. What a huge place. To be honest, we felt totally lost at first. We got tickets on the door (easy enough) but then once in, we couldn't get alipay or WeChat to work to buy tickets for the sightseeing shuttle... We paid in cash which they accepted thankfully (even though the guy on the queue didn't tell us this for 20 mins while we kept trying and failing to use the app). Anyway, we made it to Villa 6 and queued up for an hour to see 2 pandas very briefly, but were then able to walk through other areas where we saw them so easily and closely. If I was to go again, I wouldn't queue for any of the villas and id just walk through the villa areas and nurseries instead. The red pandas were cute too. It was super busy in the morning but felt much quieter by 1pm and further into the park.

This place is huge, bring your walking shoes. Many pandas to see. There are also shuttle buses that help move you around the park. We queued for around 2 hours to see Hua Hua who is like the celebrity panda as we didn’t really know what the queue was for. Otherwise crowds weren’t really an issue. Food options are a bit limited and underwhelming within the park itself.

Pandas EVERYWHERE, truly an incredible experience!! Awesome to see in their natural habitat and them roaming around and also just laying flat. Park is huge beyond just the main panda villa area as well, worth at least half a day
A really brilliant place to see Panda's. Juat get tgere early and go to the West gate as all the crowds enter via the South gate.

Very well maintained place with lots of pandas and other kinds of bears. Advice to buy the tickets in advance on either wechat or alipay apps. Doors opens at 7.30 in the morning but by 6.45 itself people start to queue up for entry. There are two queues one for the Chinese nationals with national id card and other for foreigners with passports. Once passport and ticket cross check done after 7.30, you will see throngs of people rush to enclosure 6 where the most popular panda is. The queue to view this panda is really super long. There are other enclosures which also provide close up viewing of the pandas. Suggest to visit the facility in the morning as the pandas are fed at 8am and you can see them munching on bamboos.
lots of pandas, went in the afternoon. Recommended to go in morning instead. 1430 is their feeding time when its more likely to see pandas chilling.

Place is huge and you need a long time to see all of it. When we visited, a number of places were under construction. It is better to visit in winter, as the pandas are all outdoors. In the summer and warmer months the pandas are kept inside in air conditioned rooms. They are lazy animals, every single one we saw was asleep and motionless haha. Parts of the park are insanely crowded with people jamming up against you or pushing to take a photo of a single sleeping panda, and there are security personnel everywhere to make sure everyone behaves. You will be surprised, how many people are prone to bad behavior! 🤣 The red panda exhibits were a bit more fun to watch as they are more active and adorable.

Visiting the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding was an unforgettable experience. Nestled among lush bamboo forests, this incredible sanctuary offers a unique opportunity to see adorable black-and-white giants in an environment that closely resembles their natural habitat. From the early morning, I had the chance to watch the pandas in action: playing, munching on bamboo, and displaying their famously clumsy charm. The highlight was definitely seeing the baby pandas in their enclosures—absolutely heart-melting! The park itself is vast, with well-maintained paths and picturesque views, making it a joy to explore. In addition to the giant pandas, I also got to see red pandas, which were equally fascinating. These adorable creatures, resembling raccoons, have bright reddish fur and thick coats that help them blend into the forest. Red pandas are excellent climbers, equipped with strong claws and a special “sixth finger” on their front paws that helps them grip bamboo branches. They’re about the size of a large house cat, and their long bushy tails help them balance as they move through the trees. To get around the park, I used the shuttle buses, which turned out to be very convenient. They made it easy to travel between different areas without getting too tired from walking. However, I’d suggest that it might not be necessary to pay extra for premium services since the standard options already provide a great experience. I highly recommend visiting in the early morning when the animals are most active. This trip left me not only with immense joy from seeing these incredible creatures up close but also with a deep appreciation for their uniqueness and beauty.

This research base is a goverment funded place aimed at protecting and breeding giant pandas. There's so many of them in different enclosures. Since it's still very hot in September, all the pandas stayed indoor in an airconditioned glass enclosure where all visitors can view them at a close encounter. It's a huge area and the sanctuary has about 200 pandas. We can also see the keepers cleaning up each enclosure before the pandas come out from their cage area. Lots of bamboo shoots are placed for them to eat throughout the day. There's also baby pandas, breeding area and also a small place on information of the pandas. The sanctuary has cafes, food, souvenirs, etc spread at different area and also near the exit. This place has lift for wheelchair impaired people. There's also escalators at entrance and exit area. Even though there's shuttle bus, we did not take it as there's too many people and it will take us 1-2 hours to queue. We rather walk slowly to enjoy the sceneries and fresh air.

It's hard to believe these pandas are real animals and not just humans dressed in panda costumes. They act so humany, so relatable, lazy, lounging around, sticking to the aircons, slouching on the floor legs wide open while they munch on bamboo. All the reviews said pro tip is to come early. I will give you a pro, pro tip, go late. After 4pm is when it gets good. I'm not a morning person so I wasn't about to wake up early even for this. We got there around 2pm. First two hours we saw lots nothing, we were starting to worry we wouldn't even see sleeping pandas. Then from 4 to 7 it was panda prime time, we saw them eating, walking, fighting, pooing, peeing and playing. They didn't ask us to leave the park at 6pm (closing time). Everyone disappeared around 5 but we stayed to check out all the other sections for another 2 hours without the crowds. We spent a total of 6 hours in the park, walked 22km apparently. It was amazing 😍 N.B. the yellow and green sections on the map towards the west and east of the park are far superior to the red and blue sections near the south gate.

This is a must-visit for panda lovers! Watching these cute and adorable pandas eat, sleep, and play is such a wholesome experience. The place itself has an amazing vibe. it's clean, well-organized, decorated with panda-themed elements, and surrounded by lush greenery that reflects its conservation focus. It's a fun and memorable way to see these adorable animals up close. For the best experience, consider using the sightseeing bus, especially if you want to visit spots like Hua-Hua. Otherwise, be prepared to walk a lot!

Simply amazing … the main reason I wanted to visit that part of China was to see the pandas, and it didn’t disappoint. No baby pandas as it wasn’t the time of year, but saw HEAPS of pandas. Love the giant panda, but the red ones are super cute as well. Well marked signs and easy to navigate, don’t underestimate how large this place is. Go early, stay late! Unmissable … highly recommend!

So this place isn't, in my humble opinion, worth visiting at all. It's so very difficult to see pandas properly, you are better off visiting a local zoo that has a panda on loan. The queues of people are ridiculous. The glass on the enclosures are so incredibly filthy that you can't even see the pandas clearly let alone take photos. Out of the supposedly 200 pandas at this site, we managed to glimpse 10 over a 2 hour visit. If you want to buy panda souvenirs then give the shops in this park a big miss. They charge 2 to 3 times more than the shops outside the park or in central Chengdu.

We visited in August and, unfortunately, it was not the best experience. The queues were extremely long, and it was hard to actually see the animals. A useful tip – if you notice crowds heading in one direction, try the other side of the park. It’s less busy, and although there are fewer pandas (usually one in each area), you at least get a chance to see them without waiting for hours. The park itself is very nice, with plenty of shaded spots to rest and areas to eat. They also have unique ice creams and souvenirs, though both are a bit overpriced. Overall, the setting is beautiful, but the overcrowding made it difficult to enjoy fully.

Come early - the best for the opening hours, as pandas can be seen outside and not that many people. Tickets can be purchased over WeChat or at the entrance too. The place is really well organized and would take you around 1,5-2 hours to walk around.

In the beautiful Panda city this place is a must visit I was surprised to see so many pandas The chance to see red pandas is unique There are lot of souvenir stores outside this place I recommend you to go early morning to see pandas in the open space

It’s a massive place. Best to take the bus ride. 30Yuan each. But somehow it’s tough to navigate. Signboard somehow to me is misleading. They have a south and west gate. Bus only go 1 way and got to take note which end you are getting up and going down. Overall pandas are everywhere. Will definitely have to walk once off the bus.

Booked morning tickets on trip.com. Lots of cute pandas. In hot weather, one may only see them outside early in the morning, then they all go inside A/C glass enclosures to eat, sleep, move a bit, eat, sleep…The park is huge, the small carts ($) greatly help reduce the walking distances. There can be a lot of people, it’s best to go at opening time. One trick that we would’ve liked to try was taking the cart all the way to the last station (before the other exit), and going backwards, but we only read about it afterwards. In the end, no one can resist such adorable animals.

There are 2 entrances ~ West and South. Taxi could only take you to a nearby drop off point (car park entrance) and you have to walk for like 500m before reaching the ticket office/entrance (inaccessible by taxi). Purchase ticket in advance for entry, book online to tour the Panda Museums (scan QR code at entry), and book shuttle bus for ¥30 so you wouldn’t need to walk around the huge park under the scorching hot sun. Pandas were all hiding themselves in AC rooms sleeping or eating and none were out playing in open air.

Beautiful to watch these creatures in their beautiful enclosures (not in cages). We spent about 2,5hours walking around and learning about their habits, but I could happily have stayed for longer. The panda research base is about 10km downtown from Chengdu. Make your reservation online prior to your visit. Well worth a visit!!

Very much enjoyed my day here although there are a few things I would do differently, so hopefully others can learn from our experience. First of all, we saw more pandas than we had seen in the rest of our life combined. Such a large area with so many enclosures. However, my favorite was actually the red pandas. There were a larger number of them in a smaller area so much easier to see. They also seemed very playful and would chase each other and do other interesting behaviors. I'd be sure to swing by there. It seems like the popular areas are mostly near the south gate, so that's where most people are entering from, and that's what we did. So we first went to the more popular areas and found them to be very, very crowded, even on a weekday. We were unable to get good pictures or videos of any of the younger pandas. To me it seems like luck of the draw if you can a good shot. For example, if a panda comes out, there is a small stretch where people can capture them on camera. It's not like people in that area will take 1 picture and let the next guy in. They will take pictures and videos until the panda is gone. So pretty much only people who happened to be there at the right time could get a good shot and anyone who is a little in front or behind is out of luck. If I could do it over, I would not spend as much time in the crowded areas. After we finished with the south area, we continued on to the rest of the park, where there were a lot more pandas and a lot less people. It was a lot of walking, but it was here where we didn't have to get lucky to be in a good spot, and could take our time to get good photos. We found this part to be very relaxing and enjoyable compared to the chaos of people in the south area. After we had finished exploring, we ended up in the West gate and wanted to take the shuttle back to the south gate. The line was incredibly long and we waited for about an hour. There were no chairs to sit in while we waited so after many hours of walking, this was a disaster. I think it was a combination of people entering the park trying to go to the south area to see the younger pandas, and people like us who were done exploring and going back to the entrance where we came. If I could do it over, I would do it backward and start at the west gate and finish at the south. There should be a lot less people going from South to west when you are finished.

If you are in Chengdu and if you like the cutest of cute fuzzy animals, this should be on top of your list. I wish the ticketing and other services were more well-thought-out towards international visitors without local guides, though. The park itself is well-maintained with loads of green spaces, shops, restaurants, etc. There are multiple places to see other than pandas like a research facility, a small cinema showing videos of pandas' lifecycles, and a small museum. The park is huge so put aside enough time. Also, pandas did not seem particularly keen on showing themselves a lot. You would have to be patient to see them. But when you do see them, you are in for a treat.
Tickets were available on the same day. I would totally recommend to visit this place and plan at least 4-5 hours. Drink machines are available in the area, sanitary facilities of course as well.

I visited the Chengdu Panda Base with high hopes, eager to see these incredible animals and learn more about the conservation work being done. While it was amazing to see giant pandas up close, I left feeling heavy-hearted. Many of the pandas I saw appeared stressed, restless, and unhappy. Some were pacing repeatedly, others refused to eat, and one in particular was desperately trying to get out of a small glass cage-like enclosure. She was extremely stressed and was pacing around, knocking the locked door to be opened for her. These behaviors aren't just quirks—they're signs of distress, and it was difficult to witness. Despite the center's reputation for conservation, it felt like many pandas were simply being bred to stay in captivity, rather than prepared for a life in the wild. It raises hard questions: are these animals part of a genuine conservation effort, or are they being kept as breeding machines for display? On top of that, the environment created by some of the visitors was incredibly disrespectful. Huge amount of crowd were there, they were yelling loudly near the enclosures, smoking, and even spitting in public areas—completely inappropriate for a place that’s meant to be peaceful and respectful toward wildlife. It didn’t seem like staff were stepping in to enforce respectful behavior either. I saw nothing about conservation or research apart from some signs written in few languages. This felt more of a zoo with loads of gift shops. I believe in conservation and the protection of species like the giant panda and I appreciate that they are stopping them from going extinct but more importantly, how the animals themselves are experiencing it. This place has potential, but there needs to be more transparency, better crowd control, and a stronger commitment to the mental and emotional well-being of the animals, not just their physical survival. These are giant animals and need more space and more mental stimulation. I hope others visit with open eyes—and hearts.
They are super cute. The place is very huge, toilets clean. (I visit on weekday)

The Panda Bear has been China's national symbol since ancient times representing peace. These bears are endemic to China, and an excellent place to see the Pandas are in Chengdu. The Chengdu Research Base is located in a large area, with beautiful designed walking paths that allow the visitor the opportunity to observe the Pandas in a place that replicates their natural habitat.

We were lucky on that day (Monday morning), when there were not many people, nice weather, and charming and beautiful pandas were active outside. A must visit place in Chengdu. I also would advice to start at the South Gate, since there are not so many activities yet at the West Gate.

Enjoyed this extensive panda zoo park. Grounds are very well maintained, and pandas very active when we were there in the cool March morning. The facilities and landscaping were very nice. Only the enclosure to the popular panda Hwa Hwa was 1hr long. We skipped it. There was plenty of others to enjoy. Note that the park is huge, so either buy the tram ticket or be prepared to walk a lot. Overall recommended.
When you're in Chengdu, Its Panda city so you gotta check out this research facility park. Its a must.

The Chengdu Panda Reserve is China's official Panda breeding park with some 100 pandas living there. They are considered a national treasure and are.loaned to zoo's all over the world under strict conditions. A memorable experience and a must-visit place in Chengdu
Chengdu's weather still so hot in September. Most of the pandas sleeping when we visited. Still cute though.
These pandas are so cute. They are resting most of the time. This is one of the best place in Chengdu.

The Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding is indeed a popular destination, and booking tickets in advance is highly recommended to avoid long wait times. Tips for Visiting the Chengdu Panda Research Base 1. *Book tickets in advance*: Purchase tickets online or through a reputable tour operator to ensure availability. 2. *Visit early*: Arrive at the research base early in the morning to see the pandas when they're most active. 3. *Plan around panda schedules*: Pandas typically eat and play in the morning, and rest or sleep by 11 am. 4. *Wear comfortable shoes*: The research base is large, and you'll want to be comfortable while walking around. 5. *Respect the animals*: Keep a safe distance, don't touch or feed the pandas, and follow instructions .

Great display of pandas. If you want to skip the tiresome walk of going from one display to another, just go to the panda reception hall, it's a long strip of pandas that are playing with their cubs. The pandas are typically hiding in the panda villas. The red panda nursery was also great since you can be very near the red pandas. It's also not as crowded. I honestly enjoyed the red panda exhibit more than the giant pandas.

The Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding is a remarkable institution dedicated to the conservation and breeding of giant pandas. Situated in Chengdu, China, this research base plays a crucial role in safeguarding the endangered giant panda population. The facility provides a conducive environment for pandas, simulating their natural habitat while ensuring their well-being. Visitors have the unique opportunity to witness these iconic creatures up close, observing their playful antics and learning about their habits. The base's commitment to research extends beyond breeding, contributing valuable insights into panda behavior, nutrition, and overall health. The professionalism and dedication of the staff at the Chengdu Research Base are commendable. They are knowledgeable about panda conservation and eagerly share information with visitors. The educational programs offered here contribute to raising awareness about the importance of protecting these beloved animals. The base also actively engages in international collaborations, furthering global efforts for giant panda conservation. The picturesque landscapes and well-maintained enclosures make the visit a memorable experience. Overall, the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding stands as a beacon of hope for giant panda conservation, successfully combining education, research, and breeding in a captivating and informative manner.

I visited this research station on a weekday morning. Unfortunately, it was very busy with other visitors, but I had expected that in advance. People were pushing and squeezing at the various pavilions, so that you didn't always get a good view of the animals. It only was possible with a lot of patience to observe the pandas without being disturbed. At the breeding station, where you could see young ones, I didn't stand in the queue, because there were way to many other people waiting in line. Perhaps the management should consider not letting too many people in at the same time, also because of consideration for the animals. However, overall I have to say that I really liked this facility with the very rare giant and red pandas and I took home more good impressions than bad ones.

This was one of the highlights of my trip to China to visit the research base for Pandas. Firstly it is quite a vast area and requires quite a bit of walking through numerous Panda enclosures including those for red pandas. It is quite crowded and it might be difficult to view the Pandas with the crowds, in addition to the fact that sometimes the Pandas may not be in easily visible locations within their enclosures. Be ready to spend a few hours here. The work they do here and how well organized it is is truly amazing.

Very big place. Panda are active and eating in morning so is best to go in morning. There’s 2 gate west and south. South Gate is nearer to the famous Hua Hua. There’s direct express bus to the base can use Alipay to pay for ticket before boarding. Might be better to go from south to west and queue to catch Hua Hua before visiting the other pandas. But I do believe it’s packed in morning from south to west. As it’s winter just skip the breeding and nursery to save time. Bought ticket on trip.com but it doesn’t work. Had to request refund and buy ticket.

This place has potential but was disappointing compared to my high expectations. I thought I would see pandas in non-zoo like habitats, like San Diego Zoo’s safari park. I found the crowds challenging. It was a hot and humid July day and the mass of sweaty bodies pushing to get views and photos was too much for me. I also was disappointed by the nursery, as the blinds were drawn on baby pandas taking a nap, so I didn’t see any babies. Couldn’t they have one way glass or something so we could still see? I also felt the educational signs lacking, at least in English. I only read a few that were informative (about 2 color vision, about strength of panda jaw muscles). Nothing that I read described the habitat of pandas or reintroduction plans. They lost an opportunity to educate folks on environmental issues. Instead the center just used it to show off cuddly pandas. To be honest, the panda viewing experiences I’ve had in US were better due to lack of jostling crowds. We visited in a Thursday in early July.

In oct/nov pandas are generally visible in the early morning and around 4-5p. They prefer cooler days so on hot days you might not see many. We saw maybe a dozen pandas or more this morning, some were eating, playing with one another, wandering around the enclosure. The bamboo forest that you get to walk around is really nice too. Better to not come in the summer or high season, crowds can form quickly trying to take pictures and there is also currently a 2-3hr line to see the famous Hua Hua

A great place to see pandas, as this is a closer place to city center vs other pandas conservation locations. It's a lot like a zoo with pandas. It's quite big which allows walking around into different enclosures to see the pandas. There is also the enclosed area where pregnant pandas, young and baby pandas are kept. The newly born is no bigger than a squirrel but they grew fast. The young pandas in the crib can be entertaining as they are learning how to crawl and climb out of the crib. Tip: try to get there around feeding time where the pandas will be active, as after they are full they tend to fall asleep - many wedge themselves between tree branches like giant koalas.

This park is very big. It houses a lot of Giant pandas and also red pandas(Chinese call them little pandas). Tickets about CNY¥55+-. Pandas prefer cold climate, avoid visiting in summer. Visiting the giant Panda cubs takes about 2 hours of line. FAINT.

I visited the Chengdu Panda Base on a Friday morning. By 7:30 AM, I was already in line with hundreds of other visitors. It is necessary to book your tickets via the app at least a day in advance. Have a Chinese friend or a hotel concierge make the booking for you, as you will need local language skills and a local mobile number. At the gate, your booking will be verified using your passport number. The entrance fee is 55 yuan per adult. The research base itself is an incredible experience, though it is always very crowded. Plan to spend at least 3-4 hours at the base to fully enjoy everything it has to offer. Once you get used to the crowds, it becomes a truly enjoyable visit.

Really fun seeing the pandas back in 2018. Was lucky enough to see the new born Pandas that were only a few weeks old. I must warn you to wear long sleeve and use lots of mosquito repellent as they will eat you alive. Seriously they've got no chill! Take precautions or you will leave looking like a dot to dot. Other then that I would definitely recommend visiting.

Queue time about 20 minutes to enter the panda base. There are many places where we can see giant pandas, but we discovered that the moon sanctuary was the best with closer distance, and we observed about 10 pandas there. Sun sanctuary and other places were too crowded, and we hardly could have space to stand. There are many photo spots inside the park. The panda post office near the entrance and tourist centre was interesting. There are many panda stamps for my panda collection booklet. There is another panda post office outside the park. Here, I also got many panda stamps and were able to buy a postcard to mail to our home country. It takes about 10 days to reach our home in Malaysia

Omg, what an amazing experience for our group of five! We live in California, so visiting Chengdu and going to the panda sanctuary was a dream come true. We were pleasantly surprised by how big the facility was, spending the entire day walking around the different sections. The pandas were out and about, and we saw them eating, playing, falling out of trees, and relaxing. We even saw the baby pandas! It was such an incredible experience. The ticket price was reasonable as well. Definitely something you do not want to miss if visiting Chengdu. The research center is great for all ages! Just be prepared for a lot of walking!

I respect the work of preservation that is being done by the teams that work here (and they explain it well in the museum), but for the visitor this is more a zoo than a preservation center. Animals have little space like any other zoo. You will see a lot of pandas but I don’t believe this is done in a respectful way for the animals.
Quite big place but honestly it's quite hard to see the panda and red panda because of the crowd. They also often hiding inside but it's still worth it to go if you visit ChengDu.

One of the best ways to spend the day watching these incredibly cute things going about their daily life. It's worth going in the morning as this is when most feeding seems to occur which means that the pandas, who are normally incredibly lazy and sleep most of the time, actually move around and eat. This place is mostly for giant panda but also includes a number of red panda which are also very cute. Is easy to reach by taking the metro to the Panda avenue stop then jumping on one of the many buses which are waiting there.

Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding is much larger than a typical British zoo and the animals look to be in very good health both physically and mentally. However, the pictures don't reflect the experience of viewing the animals very well. You don't get to see them interacting naturally as if in the wild. Instead, the animals are fed in a sparse concrete room with a glass wall, the other side of which are a thousand tourists banging on the glass.

Once we arrived at the first enclosure, we realised a couple of things. Firstly, one of the biggest reason why you should visit Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地) is because you won’t be able to see anywhere else in the world, 3 or more pandas playing together in the same sanctuary. This is because China usually loans a pair of pandas to host countries. Hence, it is a sight to behold, seeing 3 teenage pandas rolling about and playfully “attacking” and “challenging” each other in the enclosure. Speaking of which, if you don’t already know – all the pandas in the world belong to China. The only exception is Xin Xin, a giant panda living at the Chapultepec Zoo in Mexico City who is a descendent of a pair of pandas gifted to UK in the 70s/80s. Which means that in the future, when Xin Xin passes on, all the pandas in the world would officially belong to China. Secondly, there are so many pandas at the Giant Panda Research Base in Chengdu that you’ll be able to see pandas of different sizes and age. From infants to teenagers and adults, you’ll be able to see them all at one go right here at the Chengdu Panda Research Centre For more details, visit 2bearbear today!

The environment that the pandas reside in mimics their natural habitat; which is better than most zoos that I've visited. I loved the views that the center had to offer. However, some parts of the center can get a bit crowded. Overall, it's an experiance that is worth travelling to during a stay in China.

If you love Pandas, this is the place to see them up close. They are so adorable but really lazy. All they do is chew on bamboos, sleep and poop, lol. The park is quite walk-able so you do not need to pay and get the shuttle ride which has long lines and realistically not needed. Cost of park was very reasonable, sometime like $10usd. Unfortunately, there was no birthing of Pandas at the time we where there as it would of been very cool to see.

There are so many pandas here, which is good because they sleep like 14 hours a day so you have a good chance of seeing them do something lol. Also the only other place you'll see foreigners probably :p Even if you don't care so much for pandas it's also just a really nice park to walk around in.
The park was a bit disappointing. You definitely have to go early otherwise you won’t see any pandas at all. It was a nice trip and probably a must do but I expected more :(

I’d recommend visiting in the winter. In the summer it gets really hot and humid, and the pandas head indoors as early as 9am, so you don’t get to see much. And the place gets super crowded. Even if you buy a sightseeing bus ticket, you still end up waiting in long lines just to get on. Honestly, the experience in summer can feel a bit underwhelming.

First time visit to the Panda Research Base. Excellent experience well worth the road trip. We were blessed with good weather and managed to catch a good view of the Pandas. Better to go with a group tour, as the guide will be able to guide you around the park and save some time trying wayfind. Arrvie early to avoid long queues at the entrance and to see the pandans. Foreigners do remember to bring your passport for verification.

Visited during CNY (1/FEB/2025) - There are lots of cute pandas, but also lots of people. - Expect groups to skip lines and expect to get yelled at if you call them out ((the staff at the tour bus station did not help manage the situation at all. - Make sure to carry cash with you because the tour bus ticketing system goes down when the network is too busy. - You will need a pretty good camera to zoom in to actually see the super star pandas clearly
A must visit park when you visit cheng du. You’ll get up close to giant pandas and pandas in a beautiful natural park. According to locals - Must visit during cold weather for more active pandas.

DON'T GO IN THE HOT MONTHS! all the pandas are in their air-conditioned concrete houses before even June. Their thermostat was set to 22°C so if it's constantly under 22 outside when you go you may be fine. Also, the red pandas and monkey exhibits were closed. it was hard to find pandas!... weird. I'm sure this park is great during the cooler months but this was my experience hence the 1-star.

The centre is certainly worth a visit as it is the easiest way to see a panda up close - and all ages of panda. The centre is a bit of a mix between panda theme park / zoo and breeding centre - it wasn't clear how many of the panda bred here are released in the wild? Hopefully, none of the ones we saw as they were far to familiar with people for release. The pandas themselves were classic cute and cuddly, either playing with each other, sleeping or eating - all were classic photo opportunities. Also kept at the centre are Red panda, presumably part of a breeding program too? You can get really close to both species. Certainly is a must visit, but there are also questions about how much it contributes to wild giant panda or red panda conservation in the field.
The Panda base is the one must-see attraction in Chengdu. Panda is more active in the morning . It is a huge base , and we need to walk a lot . Option to buy buggy ticket to round the whole area .

Literally this is best place in the WORLD to see pandas. They have hundreds. And pandas are native to this area in Sichuan. I would say that it's A MUST SEE. Not only is it a marvel to conservationism, but I would argue that it's one of the best (and cutest!) Prides of China. It was very easy to get there by Subway system. After arriving at Panda Avenue, we took a bus there which was about a 7 minute drive. DEFINITELY would recommend coming early. As early as possible. Around 10~12 crowds of people show up and if it's hot outside the pandas will be inside and literally everyone and their children will push against you to take a picture, especially if the pandas are awake and moving. To see the newborns expect a line, no matter how early. But the babies are literally the most precious and adorable things on the planet!!!!!! I thought that it was very worth it, and an amazing experience. I've also been told that sometimes the red pandas walk around outside of their habitats. They do have tour guides who speak English, if you want. They have tall bamboo coverings along the paths to help shade the guests. Sometimes can be a bit of a walk, but they have mini buses to help transport people if you're willing to wait for one. But overall 10/10 would go again!

We reached slightly before 8am on a weekend and the queue to enter was quick. Tip is to come before 10am as the weather gets too warm and the pandas will not stay outdoors. There are many street vendors selling cute panda headbands outside the attraction (5~10 CNY). The panda ice cream was surprisingly nice too (16CNY each)

Book your ticket and own tour guide on ctrip if you don’t have a local mobile line. Much cheaper and faster, taking a didi from city centre to the place takes 30mins or less, very much doable. Recommend if you like pandas- the tour guide comes with interesting stories which is bettter than if you walk and explore on your own. Instructions and introduction comes in both mandarin and English.
A very spacious park for giant and red pandas. The crowds were insane even early in the morning. Make sure get your tickets in advance. Prepare to walk alot and see the cute fluff balls.

One of the best place i have visited , it is recommended that you should buy ticket online and reach destination as early as possible, this will help in 2 ways one avoiding the crowd and second is you will see pandas awake 😄 . It's a very huge facility so you need to go for golf cart which is very cost effective and easy for travel inside the park. Panda house / bamboo house is a must place to visit followed by some food inside . Not to miss is the soft toys as sovinair

Tickets are $8, and buses in the base are $4. It is recommended not to go in summer, because giant pandas are not active outdoors in summer. The base is very large. In addition to watching pandas, it is also suitable for people who like to walk, The souvenir shop can use visa cards, and there are direct buses at the gate of the base to other scenic spots!

Truly a once in a lifetime experience. We took a shuttle from the subway, which was included in the ¥55 entrance ticket bought at the shuttle station. The shuttle station can be found just outside Panda avenue subway station (line 3), the first shuttle leaves at 7:50. So we arrived at the Panda base at around 8:10 Because we arrived before most people we didn’t have to queue once or stand in line to see any of the pandas, the later it got though the busier the base got so we would recommend going to see the cubs at the two nurseries first. We saw around 40 pandas that day including 11 cubs. Also plan your trip in the cooler months because pandas are kept indoors when temperatures are high.

The park is truly breathtaking and definitely worth a full day's visit given its vastness. Utilizing the shuttle service is highly recommended. The pandas are well cared for and a delight to observe. If you are going to see the pandas during the warmer days do expect the outdoor ones to be hiding, pandas are active when it’s cold. We purchased our tickets at the cash-only counter upon arrival at the west gate. Interestingly, it seems starting at the west gate isn't the norm. Exploring attractions near the west entrance proved to be hassle-free and less crowded, however we missed seeing the renowned HUA HUA, located at the South Gate, as she had already concluded her day (下班了） according to its caretakers when we reached her section around 3 pm. Don't forget to pick up some panda souvenirs on your way out to show your support for these magnificent creatures!

Heard that it would have been great on a nice day. But pandas do not come out on rainy or hot days. Today was raining quite a bit so unfortunately didn’t get the best view of many pandas. However got lucky with an up close encounter with a red panda which made it all worth it. Recommendation - come on a nice day that isn’t raining or too hot

We had such a lovely time at the panda research center! We got there in the morning (around 8:30am) by cab and managed to avoid the crowds and have plenty of panda time for pictures and videos. The pandas are as cute, lively, active and fun as you may have heard! We made the mistake of standing in a very long queue for Hua Hua, a sort of celebrity panda in China, and that took forever. So if you're not particularly interested in Hua Hua, there are plenty more pandas ahead! We considered the coffee shop and restaurant at the complex but decided to skip because the food looked sad and was very expensive.

Quality experience and very cheap! I was shocked by the price of the research base, extremely affordable. Didi was struggling to find drivers, although I’m not sure if that was a regular issue in Chengdu. I recommend going as early as possible, we went as soon as they opened. As the morning progressed it got busier and busier and therefore it was harder to get a good view of the pandas. The best moment was early on when we had a view of Fu Wa without any other tourists nearby, eating bamboo. I feel like the pandas are treated well at the research base as opposed to those in a zoo, they have plenty of space. If you pretend to look at something in the trees other tourists will join you because they think that you can see something, which is funny to do. Ice cream was good. If you collect novelty stamps from tourist locations they have some located in the post office! (Where you can’t actually post anything, unfortunately.) A lot of the time you are walking around trying to find pandas, which I sort of expected, but do not expect a zoo type format. Most pandas go to sleep in the afternoon after they’ve eaten.

A big park and the must visit in Chengdu since Panda is the main mascot. To get here, there are both private and public buses to this park. Within the park, it is possible to walk but the park is quite large so do be prepared so stay a whole day if you plan to visit the different panda enclosures. There are also shuttle buses going around but you would have to purchase a pass for it. It is more of luck to see which pandas are out and about, but it is a huge park so you should be able to spot some. There are also the more popular spots where it requires queueing, which you will be able to find more information online. Do take that into account if you aim to finish everything in a day.

Overall, the whole place was excellent. Well run, easy to follow and the stars of the show didn't disappoint. Pandas are generally more active when the weather is colder, so when we visited at 9AM, it also coincided with their meal time so they were very active. The main attractions are the three nurseries, Star, Sun, and Moon, and Hua Hua (花花) who's at No.6. Check out the map and plan your strategy. Here are a few suggestions (assuming you're visiting early): 1. Get the park shuttle bus. This should be a no brainer. It allows you to go both directions. 2. Break the park into sections. The adult exclosures near the South gate are an obvious cluster. From enclosure 1 you can then walk north to the plaza which would be the second cluster. 3. You'll need to decide whether to start from West Gate or South Gate. I'm not sure if there's an obvious advantage for one over the other. Going into South gate first might mean the queue for Hua Hua is shorter before the crowd starts piling on by late morning. 4. Decide where you want to have lunch. The best option would be to pack your own lunch because the park really only has F&B offerings near South gate and at the plaza.

The place was beautiful! Amazing how clean the entire park was. Although we saw most of the rears of the pandas but there was 1 particular red panda which worked very hard in entertaining all the visitors. Definitely a place to visit if you are in Chengdu. Do take note that the park is huge. So if you have young children. They do rent portable "strollers" at the entrance once you enter.

That place is more than „must see”. It was great pleasure to see real Pandas. It is like cherry on a cake during the visit in Chengdu. You can have walk in forst with wonderful smell. You can get rest in cafes. You can buy gifts. We arrived at 7:30, the queue was very long already but when gate was opened, queue was movi g very smooth. We didn’t wait long to get in.

We went on a weekday and it was packed in the southern section of the park (where the most popular panda, Hua Hua, lives). Not wanting to wait for 2 hours in line for one panda, we walked around the area including the sunshine delivery house and saw several pandas, but also lots of crowds and guards yelling over megaphones. It was a hot day, so by noon, all of the pandas were relocated to the inside enclosures. In the afternoon, we walked over to the west section of the park (panda enclosures with Moon names). All the pandas were indoors, but there were *zero* crowds, which was insane in comparison to the other half of the park which was jammed with people. If I were to go again, I’d highly recommend starting at the West entrance and seeing those pandas while outside and avoiding the crowds. I’m sure Hua Hua is cute but I’m not sure she’s worth hours of standing in the sun for a 30 second glimpse!

You should come from West gate and follow the red line they drew on the map (it may take 3-4 hours walking if you follow it). It no crowd at west gate and you can see pandas very close. Don't forget to go in the morning or you only see pandas sleeping.

Big park, well maintained , clean, alot of security around, more to remind you to keep your voices down near panda enclosure. West entrance has better transport, there are direct buses, though they will try and sell stuff which you maybe buying anyway...from Chengdu, its 10 RMB per person The pavilions and panda enclosures are much newer and more pandas to see too. Cubs are not on display, and it's best to come early, as by midday most pandas are sleeping. Red pandas are nearer South entrances. Would suggest get a Didi or taxi to South entrance and make your way up to exit thru West entrance, don't forget to get your panda stamps at the post office about 15 mins away from West entrance.
An attraction in Chengdu that can't be missed. The pandas are really adorable. If you are going for Hua Hua, her enclosure is closed on Mondays. She is usually active in the early morning.

(Visited August 2017) Had the opportunity to see baby pandas days old in incubators! Many babies were playing with each other in different areas. Was excited to have seen them as active as they were. The Red Pandas are the cutest! A couple were out and about walking their “paths” soaking up the sun. Look like little kudamundies. Nice concession areas for a quick break and refreshments. Nice place for families but walking is a lot so wear your comfy shoe and stroller a good idea for littles ones. Only negative would be the amount your walking and through very steep hills at times.

Spacious research base where you could take the whole day wondering around. Plenty of pandas to see. There is not much food sold inside so it’s better to prepare some snack with you. Super clean toilets! And different transportation modes available if you don’t like walking!

you are going to love it. ignore those salty travellers. It is that great.. Me and my family was visitting here from 8 am to 4 pm and we still cant get enough. Its that huge, the animals mostly visible and the place is clean and there is no bad odors

Please go as early as possible as it get very crowded after 830am (I reached at 8am but it got very crowded slightly after that). The traffic arrangement could have been better, especially at the panda nursery area. You would be able to see quite many pandas here. To me, it's a been there done that trip if you are in Chengdu. Do bring raincoat/umbrella if it's raining as most visiting area are outdoor (or you can get a raincoat at 10yuan illegally sold near the entrance)

Great Place to visit with family n friends who enjoy looking at panda 🐼.. ( *Remark : Wear comfortable walking shoes ) The whole place is huge...so will spend alot of time here if anyone wish to see the whole place.. Whoever wishes to visit this place MUST come early morning when the place is open...partly because most of the panda with be more lively early morning when caretaker feeding them....after that the pandas 🐼 will be hidden or sleeping 😴... We don't get to see the red panda n even the small pandas..because is closed on weekdays... Just follow the crowd to know when the panda is hidden..

The cuteness of these adorable pandas cannot be explained in words. They are the true teddy bears. The research center is huge and very nicely maintained for visitors. One can find many pandas here for sure. Really enjoyed my time there.

One of the best ways to spend the day watching these huge cute creatures. It's preferable to vist it in the morning to see the active Pandas moving around and eat. since they are incredibly lazy and sleep most of the time, but if you can't make it in the morning, try to spend more time there and you'll see them active at some point. This place is huge, I highly recommand wearing comfy clothes ans shoes to be able to move around and stand for longer periods. Also, it's China! Expect long queues especially during weekends and holdays is.

Wow! What an amazing experience. This review was a long time coming, but nonetheless the memories are so clear. Absolute highlight of my trip to Chengdu and these pandas are just lovable.
